extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary and secondary schools, postsecondary institutions, and other recipients), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, investigators, decision-makers, and legal/compliance counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory requirements (34 CFR part 106, §§106.30, 106.44, 106.45, etc.) describing definitions, duties, procedural rules, recordkeeping, notice, and training that recipients must follow when responding to reports and formal complaints of sexual harassment in education programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures means non-disciplinary, non-punitive individualized services offered as appropriate, as reasonably available, and without fee or charge to the complainant or the respondent before or after the filing of a formal complaint or where no formal complaint has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such measures are designed to restore or preserve equal access to the recipient's education program or activity without unreasonably burdening the other party; examples include counseling, extensions of deadlines, modifications of work or class schedules, campus escort services, mutual restrictions on contact, changes in work or housing locations, leaves of absence, increased security and monitoring, and other similar measures. The recipient must maintain as confidential any supportive measures provided to the complainant or respondent, to the extent that maintaining such confidentiality would not impair the ability to provide the measures. The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the effective implementation of supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice of allegations upon receipt of a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a formal complaint, a recipient must provide written notice to the parties who are known informing them of the recipient's grievance process and the allegations being investigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include sufficient details known at the time and with sufficient time to prepare a response before any initial interview; sufficient details include the identities of the parties involved (if known), the conduct allegedly constituting sexual harassment under §106.30, and the date and location of the alleged incident (if known). The written notice must state that the respondent is presumed not responsible, inform parties they may have an advisor of choice (who may be an attorney), inform parties they may inspect and review evidence, and inform them of any code of conduct provision prohibiting knowingly making false statements. If additional allegations arise during investigation, the recipient must provide notice of the additional allegations to known parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients who wish to offer parties the option of informal resolution of formal complaints may do so only after providing written notice and obtaining voluntary, written consent from the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice must disclose the sexual harassment allegations, the requirements of the informal resolution process, and any consequences from participating in the informal resolution process. Informal resolution may be used to resolve allegations in a formal complaint without completing investigation and adjudication, but recipients may not offer or facilitate informal resolution to resolve allegations that an employee sexually harassed a student. Participation is voluntary and requires written consent. Recipients should create or modify forms to document notice and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements and seven-year retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain certain documentation regarding Title IX activities for seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records to be retained include sexual harassment investigations (including determinations regarding responsibility and any required audio/audiovisual recordings or transcripts), disciplinary sanctions imposed, remedies provided to restore or preserve equal access, appeals and their results, any informal resolution, materials used to train Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and informal resolution facilitators, and records of actions (including supportive measures) taken in response to reports or formal complaints. For each response required under §106.44(a), recipients must document the basis for its conclusion that its response was not deliberately indifferent and document measures taken to restore or preserve equal access. If supportive measures are not provided, documentation must include reasons why such a response was not clearly unreasonable under the circumstances. The Department uses these records to assess prevalence of harassment and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient's general response duty (promptness and not deliberately indifferent)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient with actual knowledge of sexual harassment must respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient is deliberately indifferent only if its response is clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances. A recipient's response must treat complainants and respondents equitably by offering supportive measures to complainants and by following a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before imposing disciplinary sanctions or other actions that are not supportive measures against a respondent. The Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact the complainant to discuss supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes, inform of availability with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint. The Department will not deem compliance satisfied by restricting constitutional rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to a formal complaint must follow §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a formal complaint, a recipient must follow a grievance process that complies with §106.45; with or without a formal complaint, recipients must comply with §106.44(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assistant Secretary will not deem a recipient's determination regarding responsibility to be evidence of deliberate indifference solely because the Assistant Secretary would have reached a different determination based on independent weighing of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may remove a respondent from the education program or activity on an emergency basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before emergency removal the recipient must undertake an individualized safety and risk analysis, determine that an immediate threat to the physical health or safety of any student or other individual justifies removal, and provide the respondent with notice and an opportunity to challenge the decision immediately following the removal. Emergency removal does not modify rights under IDEA, Section 504, or the ADA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative leave for non-student employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may place a non-student employee respondent on administrative leave during the pendency of a grievance process that complies with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not modify rights under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act or the Americans with Disabilities Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and notification of Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must designate and authorize at least one employee as the Title IX Coordinator and notify relevant persons of the coordinator's contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must notify applicants for admission and employment, students, parents or guardians of K-12 students, employees, and unions or professional organizations of the name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the Title IX Coordinator. Any person may report sex discrimination (including sexual harassment) in person, by mail, telephone, or electronic mail, or by any other means that results in the Title IX Coordinator receiving the report; reports may be made at any time, including non-business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of policy and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify persons entitled to notice that the recipient does not discriminate on the basis of sex and must publish and prominently display contact information and the nondiscrimination policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must state that the nondiscrimination requirement extends to admission and employment (unless subpart C does not apply) and that inquiries may be referred to the Title IX Coordinator or the Assistant Secretary. Recipients must prominently display Title IX Coordinator contact information and the nondiscrimination policy on their website (if any) and in each handbook or catalog provided to entitled persons. Recipients must not use or distribute publications stating they treat applicants, students, or employees differently on the basis of sex, except as permitted by Title IX or this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and publication of grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must adopt and publish grievance procedures that provide for prompt and equitable resolution of complaints alleging conduct prohibited by this part and a grievance process that complies with §106.45 for formal complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide notice of their grievance procedures and grievance process, including how to report or file a complaint of sex discrimination, how to report or file a formal complaint of sexual harassment, and how the recipient will respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual knowledge means notice of sexual harassment or allegations of sexual harassment to a recipient's Title IX Coordinator or any official with authority to institute corrective measures on behalf of the recipient, or to any employee of an elementary and secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imputation of knowledge based solely on vicarious liability or constructive notice is insufficient. The mere ability or obligation to report or to inform a student about how to report, or having been trained to do so, does not qualify an individual as someone who has authority to institute corrective measures. 'Notice' includes a report to the Title IX Coordinator as described in §106.8(a). The standard is not met when the only official with actual knowledge is the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint definition and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal complaint means a document filed by a complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator alleging sexual harassment against a respondent and requesting investigation; at filing, the complainant must be participating in or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal complaint may be filed in person, by mail, or by electronic mail using the contact information for the Title IX Coordinator, and by any additional method the recipient designates. 'Document filed by a complainant' includes electronic submissions that contain the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate the complainant is the person filing. Where the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint, the Coordinator is not a complainant or party under this part and must comply with all requirements, including §106.45(b)(1)(iii) regarding conflicts of interest and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual harassment means conduct on the basis of sex that satisfies one or more of the following: (1) conditioning provision of an aid, benefit, or service on participation in unwelcome sexual conduct; (2) unwelcome conduct determined by a reasonable person to be so severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive that it effectively denies equal access to the education program or activity; or (3) sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, or stalking as defined in specified federal statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory text cites statutory definitions for sexual assault (20 U.S.C. 1092(f)(6)(A)(v)), dating violence (34 U.S.C. 12291(a)(10)), domestic violence (34 U.S.C. 12291(a)(8)), and stalking (34 U.S.C. 12291(a)(30)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(i)) — equitable treatment and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance process must treat complainants and respondents equitably by providing remedies to a complainant where responsibility is found and by following §106.45 before imposing disciplinary sanctions or other non-supportive actions against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies must be designed to restore or preserve equal access and may include individualized services similar to supportive measures; remedies may be disciplinary or punitive and need not avoid burdening the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(ii)) — objective evaluation of all relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Require an objective evaluation of all relevant evidence, including inculpatory and exculpatory evidence; credibility determinations may not be based on a person's status as complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations and determinations must assess both sides' evidence fairly and without bias tied to party status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(iii)) — neutrality, conflicts of interest, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual designated as Title IX Coordinator, investigator, decision-maker, or informal resolution facilitator must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure these individuals receive training on the definition of sexual harassment (§106.30), scope of the education program or activity, how to conduct investigations and grievance processes including hearings, appeals, and informal resolution processes, and how to serve impartially (avoid prejudgment, conflicts of interest, bias). Decision-makers must receive training on hearing technologies and issues of relevance (including when questions/evidence about sexual predisposition or prior sexual behavior are not relevant). Investigators must receive training on issues of relevance to create investigative reports that fairly summarize relevant evidence. Training materials must not rely on sex stereotypes and must promote impartial investigations and adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(iv)) — presumption of not responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination regarding responsibility is made at the conclusion of the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption must be explicit in the grievance process documentation and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(v)) — reasonably prompt timeframes and delay procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reasonably prompt time frames for conclusion of the grievance process, appeals, and informal resolution processes, and a process that allows for temporary delay or limited extension of time frames for good cause with written notice to the parties of the delay or extension and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good cause examples include absence of a party, advisor, or witness; concurrent law enforcement activity; or need for language assistance or disability accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(vi)) — description of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the range of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies or list the possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies the recipient may implement following any determination of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures should set expectations about possible outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(vii)) — standard of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the standard of evidence is the preponderance of the evidence or the clear and convincing evidence standard, apply the same standard for complaints against students and employees (including faculty), and apply the same standard to all formal complaints of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must adopt and apply a uniform standard of evidence across all categories of respondents and complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(viii)) — appeals procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the procedures and permissible bases for the complainant and respondent to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures must describe how appeals may be filed and what bases are cognizable for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(ix)) — supportive measures information
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must inform parties what individualized non-punitive services may be provided and how to request them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process requirement (§106.45(b)(1)(x)) — privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process must not require, allow, rely upon, or otherwise use questions or evidence that constitute, or seek disclosure of, information protected under a legally recognized privilege, unless the privilege holder has waived the privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must respect legally recognized privileges and may only use such privileged information if waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of formal complaints (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must investigate the allegations in a formal complaint but must dismiss for purposes of Title IX sexual harassment if the alleged conduct would not constitute sexual harassment as defined, did not occur in the recipient's education program or activity, or did not occur against a person in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient may also dismiss all or part of a formal complaint if the complainant withdraws in writing, the respondent is no longer enrolled or employed, or specific circumstances prevent collection of sufficient evidence. Upon dismissal, the recipient must promptly send written notice of the dismissal and reasons simultaneously to the parties. Dismissal for Title IX purposes does not preclude action under other provisions of the recipient's code of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of formal complaints (§106.45(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may consolidate formal complaints alleging sexual harassment against more than one respondent, or by more than one complainant against one or more respondents, or by one party against the other party, where the allegations arise out of the same facts or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation is permitted when consistent facts or circumstances underlie multiple complaints; recipients should ensure consolidation does not prejudice parties' rights.
